meta.note: Saturday special edition (quota-reset-day early run, completed before 07:15). Three headlines: Yageo plans a new MLCC hike round for late Oct-Nov (high-cap possibly +50%+, a plan not yet a formal letter) + Samsung Electro-Mechanics lead times at 52 weeks across the board; PSMC expects another 10-20% logic-foundry price hike in 2027 (LTA price lock); Microsoft attributes about $25B of capex increase to component price hikes, the Big Four clouds total ~$735B in 2026 (+79% YoY). Carrier acquires Air Temp; Trane's Cancoil deal details; Hitachi's KADENOVA deal structure; LG Multi V 7 launch; Vertiv x NVIDIA AI-factory plan. WoodMac warns of a ~1Mt aluminum deficit in 2026; Nexans says cable capacity is a new bottleneck. Events library: 12 new events (Carrier AirTemp / LG Multi V 7 / aluminum deficit / PSMC / Nexans / Microsoft NiSource / cloud capex / Korea heat pumps / Samsung Southeast Asia / BofA forecast / Zhuhai subsea compute / IREN Badajoz), 12 timeline additions (Fort Worth / Cancoil / KADENOVA / MLCC x2 / DRAM x2 / Vertiv / Rubin / industrial components / North America hikes / copper) - 53 events total.

hotspot_events.title: PSMC expects 2027 logic-foundry prices to rise another 10-20% (LTA price lock)
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Shortage spreading from memory to logic foundry + a clear LTA price-lock action window - MCU / analog chip costs affected
hotspot_events.summary: PSMC said at its Q3 earnings call that capacity is tight and expects 2027 logic-foundry prices to rise another 10-20%, locking price and volume via long-term agreements (LTAs); it already raised DRAM tape-out prices ~45% in July 2026 - the shortage is spreading from memory to logic foundry.
numbers: DRAM tape-out prices raised ~45% in July 2026

hotspot_events.title: Microsoft attributes ~$25B of capex increase to component price hikes; Big Four clouds total ~$735B in 2026 (+79% YoY)
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Quantified evidence of component hikes directly eating cloud capex + ~$735B combined confirms demand-side strength
hotspot_events.summary: Microsoft's CFO: of ~$190B calendar-2026 capex, about $25B of the increase is attributable to component price hikes (memory / networking / components); Meta raised its 2026 capex guidance to $135-145B; the Big Four total ~$735B (Amazon ~$220B, Alphabet $195-205B, Microsoft ~$175B, Meta $135-145B), +79% YoY - quantified evidence of the siphon effect.
numbers: Microsoft 2026 capex ~$190B (~$25B of the increase from price hikes)
